summary: Intermittent streaming completions cut at ~65s — ALB FIN and proxy send buffer fill correlating with SSL resumption + header growth
description:
Issue summary:
Customers report streaming completions abruptly terminate after roughly 60–70s when the client uploads the request body slowly (chunked). The connection shows ALB sending FIN and the upstream edge proxy returning 499/connection-reset symptoms. This started after the recent SSL reconfiguration that enabled session resumption and an internal change that surfaced more per-request tracing headers (baggage/traceparent rotation).

Impact:
- Multiple users of Papertrail Analytics' integration observed incomplete responses during longer-generation workflows (not every request; intermittent at ~2-5% of long streams).
- Visible customer-visible failures for live chat and transcript-generation features.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (api.redwood.ai) -> regional ALB -> edge-proxy cluster -> serving-runtime pool running redwood/gpt-large-v1 on dedicated capacity for the customer.
- Affected region: us-east-1.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a streaming completion using chunked upload with a large initial context (~120KB) and a periodic client heartbeat that appends small cookies/trace headers every 10–15s.
2) Observe TTFB is normal but after ~60–70s the stream terminates mid-completion with a connection reset.
3) Re-run with same payload but send body faster (single request) — stream completes normally.

Observed logs & signals:
- ALB connection logs show remote_close with FIN from ALB at ~65s.
- Edge-proxy metrics: per-conn send buffer high watermark triggered, proxy logged "write failed: connection reset by peer" around same time.
- Access logs carry growing Header-Length values between initial request and last chunk (from ~1.2KB up to 9.8KB).
- TLS session logs show a successful session-resumption path for affected clients.
- No direct application 5xx; serving-runtime reported no model OOM or CPU spike.

Initial hypothesis:
- Combination of slow client chunked uploads + incremental header/baggage rotation causes header size to grow mid-request, triggering proxy buffer growth and eventually exhausting the proxy send buffer or hitting ALB idle/send-timeout behavior. SSL session resumption path appears to change TCP/TLS timing such that proxy flush behavior is impacted, exacerbating the window where no bytes are sent to the ALB and triggering idle close.

Files and links shared by customer:
- pcap excerpt (sensitive) uploaded to secure case attachment.
- Example request id: req-20260301-7f2a4c.
- Slack thread: #support-papertrail (link provided).
comments: 2026-03-01 10:15 Elena Rossi (Customer): We're seeing the stream drop around the 1m mark consistently when our client streams the prompt slowly. No error text, just abrupt finish. Attaching pcap and request id.
2026-03-01 10:45 Marcus Lee (Support): Thanks Elena — triaging. Can you confirm client-side keepalive settings and whether you rotate auth tokens mid-request? Also sharing logs with SRE.
2026-03-01 11:20 SRE (Jin Park): Noted correlation with edge proxy send buffer high-water events. Related ALB logs show FIN at ~65s. Pulling proxy config and TLS metrics now.

2026-03-01 13:05 Marcus Lee: Reproduced in staging by replaying chunked upload at slow rate while rotating a trace header every 12s. Staging edge proxy hit send buffer limits and closed stream. Created INT-1342 to adjust proxy buffer tuning for reproduction.

2026-03-02 09:30 Engineering (Priya Menon): We validated that enabling session resumption changes TLS record timing; combined with repeated Set-Cookie/trace header growth we observed HPACK-like expansion on our HTTP/1.1 proxy (we're terminating TLS at the edge). Drafting a short-term mitigation: cap header size per request and drop non-essential tracing headers mid-stream.
investigation_notes: Edge proxy (nginx-flavor) configuration: proxy_buffer_size 8k; proxy_buffers 4 8k. Observed effective header bytes exceed configured buffer across some requests, triggering extra allocations and stalls.
ALB idle timeout: currently 60s for upstream idle-send; ALB will send FIN when no bytes flow for 60s despite client still uploading slowly (writes held by proxy buffer).
"Hypothesis validated in staging by synthetic client that streams body at 100B/s while rotating traceparent every 12s — reproduced identical FIN timing."
Collected metrics: proxy send buffer fill ratio, TLS record timings, header-length histogram per request.
resolution:
Workaround applied (2026-03-02): added temporary proxy rule to drop/strip non-essential tracing baggage and set conservative header-size cap for streaming routes. ALB idle-timeout raised to 120s for affected dedicated customer pool as an intermediate mitigation. Customer reported immediate reduction in truncated streaming.
Long-term fix: engineering to ship proxy buffer reconfiguration (increase proxy_buffers and enable chunked passthrough without header reassembly) and evaluate moving header enforcement earlier in the stack. Also propose a runtime change to avoid reattaching large tracing headers mid-stream. Target rollout in next maintenance window (2026-03-09).
